videos.title: You already know this one.
videos.description:
You already know this one.

It was never meant to ship. The Konami Code was debug scaffolding. It was supposed to be deleted before release.

Porting Gradius to the NES. He could not get through his own game well enough to test it, so he wrote a shortcut that handed the player every power-up at once.

What the same code granted in Contra, two years later. That is the version most people remember.

He forgot to take it out.

- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konami_Code

videos.title: One day the bug was literal.
videos.description:
One day the bug was literal. Engineers had called faults bugs since Edison. On this one afternoon, someone opened a relay and found an actual insect.

9 September. An operator traced a fault to a moth caught in a relay, removed it, and taped it into the log book instead of throwing it away.

First actual case of bug being found. Relay #70, Panel F. 15:45. The wording gives it away, they knew the joke they were making.

They kept the moth.

Sources:
- https://americanhistory.si.edu/collections/object/nmah_334663
- https://www.computerhistory.org/tdih/september/9/
- https://daily.jstor.org/the-bug-in-the-computer-bug-story/
- https://www.pricefx.com/learning-center/software-engineering-debacles-grace-hopper-and-the-first-reported-bug

videos.title: Someone had to invent cut and paste.
videos.description:
Someone had to invent cut and paste. Before it existed, moving text meant retyping it, or literally cutting the paper and pasting it down. The names are not a metaphor.

At Xerox PARC they built a text editor called Gypsy, where selecting text and moving it worked the same way every time, with no hidden mode to remember first.

In 1975 it turned up in Businessweek. In a feature called The Office of the Future. The idea was worth reporting before it was furniture.

His number plate read NO MODES.

Sources:
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_Tesler
- https://worrydream.com/refs/Tesler_2012_-_A_Personal_History_of_Modeless_Text_Editing_and_Cut-Copy-Paste.pdf

videos.title: Atari buried its games in the desert.
videos.description:
Atari buried its games in the desert. September 1983: trucks took hundreds of thousands of cartridges out to a landfill in Alamogordo, New Mexico, and buried them.

The New York Times reported it at the time. Then it slid out of the record and became a story gamers told each other, always about E.T.

All of it was true. The city, archaeologists and a film crew went ten metres down and pulled up just over 1,300 cartridges. Not only E.T.

The Smithsonian took some. So did the Henry Ford, the Strong Museum of Play and the video game museum in Rome. A landfill became a catalogued site.

The urban legend had a manifest.

Sources:
- https://core.tdar.org/project/459204/atari-dump-site-alamogordo-new-mexico-usa
- https://www.thehenryford.org/collections/explore/artifact/403653
- https://archaeology.org/issues/july-august-2014/digs-discoveries/new-mexico-atari-dump-site-excavation/

videos.title: You have never once questioned this.
videos.description:
You have never once questioned this.

It was built to slow you down. So the typebars would not jam. It is in textbooks. The researchers who traced the layout's real history called that, in print, nonsense.

At Kyoto University they followed the keyboard back past the typewriter to the telegraph. Its first heavy users were Morse operators taking down code live.

American Morse writes Z almost like S-E. An operator could not tell them apart until the following letters arrived. So S ended up next to both Z and E.

Sholes spent his last year trying to replace it.

Sources:
- http://kanji.zinbun.kyoto-u.ac.jp/~yasuoka/publications/PreQWERTY.html
- https://www.smithsonianmag.com/history/the-qwerty-keyboard-will-never-die-where-did-the-150-year-old-design-come-from-49863249/
- https://oztypewriter.blogspot.com/2012/10/on-this-day-in-typewriter-history-from.html
- https://www.britannica.com/biography/Christopher-Latham-Sholes

videos.title: Was pollinated by hand.
videos.description:
Was pollinated by hand. The orchid has its own bee only in Mexico. Everywhere else someone opens each flower and does it themselves, one at a time.

Twelve, born into slavery on Réunion and taught horticulture by the man who owned him. He saw the flower's two halves were separated by a flap you could lift.

Then more pods appeared. Bellier-Beaumont had kept one barren vine alive twenty years. In 1861 he wrote that the boy worked it out himself.

He said he taught the boy. Bellier-Beaumont checked the dates: by that account Edmond was eight. Archivists went back over it in 2009 and agreed it was his.

He died in a public hospital with nothing.

Sources:
- https://www.linnean.org/news/2019/10/16/edmond-albius
- https://www.europeana.eu/en/stories/edmond-albius
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edmond_Albius
